legend: Diagram shows the study overview. Left, the 10 datasets, grouped by whether they have a reference segmentation, with the total numbers of datasets, patients, and nodules (6715 patients and 12726 nodules). Middle, the eight segmentation configurations, grouped by the information each receives at inference: a point (nnInteractive, VISTA3D-Point, SAM-Med3D, and MedSAM2), a point and a box (PiNS), a text prompt (VoxTell), or no prompt (TotalSegmentator and VISTA3D-Auto). Each configuration returns one mask per nodule. Right, the four analyses: segmentation performance, radiomic similarity, test–retest repeatability, and downstream classification; reference masks feed every analysis except classification in the two screening datasets.

Flowchart shows the selection of patients, CT scans, and nodules in each dataset, grouped by whether the dataset has a reference segmentation. Each column starts with the dataset as released, the side box gives the exclusions with their reasons, and the shaded box gives the included set. The small boxes below give the patients (N) and nodules (n) used in each analysis, color coded as in the key: segmentation performance (blue), radiomic similarity (green), test–retest repeatability (orange), and downstream classification (purple). LNDb identifies scans only, so each LNDb CT scan is counted as one patient. The dashed box at the bottom right counts patients and nodules shared between datasets once (6715 patients, 12726 nodules): all 28 RIDER-Seg patients are QIBA patients, and three patients with the same tumor are in both QIN and LUAD-Surv. \* Nodules with a consensus mask. † Nodules with a consensus mask, after exclusion of 35 nodules whose reader masks were a single voxel. ‡ Thirty-one pairs acquired on the same day and 20 acquired months apart; one nodule had no retest scan. LUNA16 = LUng Nodule Analysis 2016.

Box and violin plots show segmentation of lung nodules by eight configurations (a) for all datasets pooled and for each dataset, and (b) pooled across datasets by nodule size and by nodule attenuation (attenuation pooled over IMD-CT, LIDC-IDRI, LNDb, and NSCLC-RG). In each panel, the upper plot shows the Dice similarity coefficient on segmented nodules (violin plot, box plot with median and interquartile range, and individual nodules), and the lower plot shows the percentage of nodules segmented, with counts. A nodule was counted as segmented when the mask had a component within 5 mm of the point or annotated center. The gray box shows inter-reader agreement on nodules with at least two radiologist outlines, and the gray italic number gives their count. In (a), hatched boxes mark datasets in all or part of the method's training data, and clean boxes mark datasets outside it; datasets for which MedSAM2 and TotalSegmentator did not disclose their training data are also shown clean but are undisclosed, not external. Brackets show paired comparisons with Holm-adjusted *P* values (top-ranked method among those that segmented at least 80% of nodules versus the second and third, and each of these three versus inter-reader agreement); in (a), brackets are shown only for datasets with at least 20 patients. In (b), 449 of 575 ground-glass and 824 of 977 part-solid nodules are from IMD-CT. *P* < .01 is the smallest value the 2000 bootstrap resamples resolve. QIN and LUAD-Surv have semiautomated reference masks.

CT images show segmentation by each configuration. Rows show, from top to bottom, a solid nodule in LNDb (5 mm), two solid nodules in LIDC-IDRI (8 and 18 mm), a nodule in QIBA (20 mm), a part-solid nodule in IMD-CT (23 mm), and a solid tumor in NSCLC-RG (71 mm). In each group, the nodule shown is the one whose mean Dice over the eight configurations (a missed nodule counted as 0) was closest to the group median. The first column shows the reference outline (consensus of radiologists in LNDb and LIDC-IDRI, white; five radiologists in QIBA, each in its own color; a reader's segmentation in IMD-CT and the expert segmentation in NSCLC-RG, white), and each other column shows one configuration's outline in color with the reference outline dashed. Each tile is an axial section through the center of the reference mask, shown with a lung window (level, −600 HU; width, 1500 HU) and a square field of view of 32 mm or 2.5 times the nodule diameter, whichever is larger; the label at the lower right gives the Dice similarity coefficient and the volume ratio (VR, method over reference volume), or "No mask" when the method had no component within 5 mm of the nodule center. The number at the upper left is the nodule diameter (maximal axial diameter of the reference mask), with the nodule attenuation below it (not recorded in QIBA).

Dot plot shows agreement of 107 radiomic features between method masks and radiologist outlines in QIBA (top), LIDC-IDRI (middle), and LNDb (bottom). Each dot shows the Lin concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) of one feature across nodules. For methods, it is the CCC between the method and each radiologist, averaged over radiologists, on the nodules the method segmented; for the inter-reader row, it is the CCC between radiologists. Dot size gives the percentage of nodules segmented. Features are grouped as shape, first order, gray-level co-occurrence matrix, run length matrix, size zone matrix, dependence matrix, and neighborhood gray-tone difference matrix; feature names are given in Figure S22. The color scale is not linear: orange marks values below 0.85, a threshold chosen before the analysis, and blue marks values above it; values below 0.40 are shown in the darkest orange. The right column gives the median inter-reader CCC or Δ (the median over features of the method's CCC minus the inter-reader CCC on the same nodules) with its 95% CI from a patient-level bootstrap, and the number of nodules segmented out of the total. VoxTell in QIBA is shown on its prespecified set of 20 nodules in eight patients outside its training data (Table 2). CI = confidence interval.

Receiver operating characteristic curves show classification by radiomic features from each mask source: malignancy in IMD-CT (histopathology), radiologist suspicion in LIDC-IDRI and LNDb, and cancer in the patient in DLCS24 (all nodules) and LUNA25-Dev. Curves use the out-of-fold probabilities of the patient-grouped fivefold cross-validation, averaged over three repeats; shaded bands are pointwise 95% CIs. Reference masks are black, the log diameter model is dashed gray, and the Lung CT Screening Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) category (DLCS24 only) is dotted black. The legend in each panel gives the AUC with its 95% CI from a patient-level bootstrap, in the order of the key. Nodules a method missed were scored at the training-fold prevalence, which produces straight segments in the curves of methods that missed many nodules. No diameter model is shown for LUNA25-Dev, which has no nodule size with a documented source. The lower right panel shows specificity at a target sensitivity of 90% (color) and the percentage of nodules segmented (dot size) for each source and dataset; Lung-RADS is omitted because its category steps cannot target 90% sensitivity. AUC = area under the receiver operating characteristic curve.

Histogram and bar charts show characteristics of the study sample, all 10 datasets combined. Top row: age (5-year bins; 5949 patients with age reported, 766 not reported), sex, race or ethnicity, and smoking status as recorded by each source (Ever\* = ever smoked, not further specified, in IMD-CT). Middle row, per CT scan: manufacturer, slice thickness (†, millimeter groups), tube voltage (three most frequent values, others combined), and reconstruction kernel (‡, names as recorded; five most frequent, others combined). The 1942 IMD-CT scans have no acquisition metadata; their slice thickness is the resampled section spacing (1.25 mm, in the 1.0–1.5 mm group), and tube voltage and kernel are not reported. Two DLCS24 scans without acquisition data are not shown in the slice thickness panel. Bottom row: nodule attenuation (recorded only in LIDC-IDRI, LNDb, IMD-CT, and NSCLC-RG) and numbers of nodules and patients per dataset. Gray bars = not reported. Per-dataset values are in Table 1 and Table S1.

Images show segmentation examples in QIN, one row per size group, chosen and displayed as in Figure S5. The reference column shows the nine semiautomated algorithm masks (three algorithms, three runs each).
Images show segmentation examples in LUAD-Surv, one row per size group, chosen and displayed as in Figure S5. The reference is the semiautomated region-growing mask.

Violin and box plots compare the same VISTA3D network run with a point (VISTA3D-Point) and without one (VISTA3D-Auto). Top: Dice similarity coefficient on nodules segmented in both modes (violin plot, box plot with median and IQR, and individual nodules), with the median paired difference (no point minus point), its 95% CI from a patient-level bootstrap, and the number of nodules. Bottom: percentage of all nodules segmented in each mode, with counts. IQR = interquartile range.

Bar chart shows the mean Dice similarity coefficient by dataset and method with missed nodules counted as 0, with 95% CIs from a patient-level bootstrap. The dot gives the mean Dice on segmented nodules only, so the gap between bar and dot reflects the proportion missed. Numbers after each dataset name are nodules.

Violin and box plots show exploratory subgroup results: (a) LIDC-IDRI slice thickness and reconstruction kernel; (b) scanner manufacturer in LIDC-IDRI and scanner model in LNDb (all Siemens); (c) IMD-CT sex, age, smoking status, and emphysema; (d) upper lobe versus other lobes in IMD-CT and LNDb; (e) spiculation in LIDC-IDRI, LNDb, and IMD-CT; and (f) PET uptake in IMD-CT. In each panel, the upper plot shows the Dice similarity coefficient on segmented nodules and the lower plot the percentage segmented (Seg.), with counts. Gray boxes show inter-reader agreement where nodules had two or more radiologist outlines, with their count in gray italics. Spiculated = mean or median reader rating of 3 or more (LIDC-IDRI, LNDb) or recorded as present (IMD-CT). No statistical tests were performed; numbers, including size-matched and solid-only rows, are in Figure S15. PET = positron emission tomography.

Heat map shows exploratory subgroup results for inter-reader agreement and the eight methods. Cells give the median Dice similarity coefficient on segmented nodules (bold; color, orange below 0.5 and blue above), the percentage of nodules segmented (upper right), and the 95% CI of the median from a patient-level bootstrap with 2000 resamples (second line); the number after each subgroup is the number of nodules. Inter-reader agreement = median pairwise Dice between radiologists (NA where a dataset has one reference segmentation per nodule); – = no nodule segmented. Rows labeled with a size group or attenuation type are restricted to those nodules. Slice thickness, kernel, and manufacturer are from the DICOM headers, with kernels grouped as soft (GE STANDARD or SOFT; Siemens B or I 40 or lower; Philips A or B; Toshiba FC1–FC19) or sharp (GE BONE, BONEPLUS, LUNG, EDGE, or DETAIL; Siemens 45 or higher; Philips C, D, E, or L; Toshiba FC50 or higher). Spiculated as in Figure S14. Manufacturers with fewer than 20 patients are not shown (LIDC-IDRI, Toshiba, five series). No statistical tests were performed; results for other size groups and attenuation types are available with the study code (Data and Code Availability in the main article). PET = positron emission tomography.

Heat map shows feature agreement in datasets with one reference or with algorithm references, from top: IMD-CT, NSCLC-RG, LNDb against one radiologist on all nodules, LUAD-Surv (semiautomated reference), and QIN, with agreement between the reference algorithms as the comparison row (10 nodules). Each cell is the Lin concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) of one feature (names at top); gray cells mark fewer than five nodules segmented. The right column gives the median CCC over features (Δ for QIN) with its 95% CI from a patient-level bootstrap and the number of nodules segmented out of the total. NSCLC-RG was in the training data of most methods (Table S2). Colors as in Figure 5.

Heat map shows the test–retest intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC; two-way random effects, absolute agreement, single measurement) of each of 107 radiomic features, with feature names, for the manual reference and the eight methods in RIDER-Seg (top; one manual contour per scan, 28 pairs), the QIBA pairs acquired on the same day (middle; five radiologists, 31 pairs), and the QIBA pairs acquired months apart (bottom; 20 pairs). The nonlinear color scale is centered at an ICC of 0.85, with orange for lower and blue for higher repeatability. The right column gives the median manual ICC or Δ ICC (median over features of the method's ICC minus the manual ICC on the same pairs) with its 95% CI from a patient-level bootstrap, and the number of pairs used out of the total. The QIBA manual rows average each radiologist's own test–retest ICC. RIDER-Seg and the QIBA same-day pairs share patients and images. A method ICC above the manual ICC does not imply greater accuracy (Figure S18). Pairs acquired months apart combine real change with measurement error.

Scatterplots show accuracy and repeatability of each method in RIDER-Seg (left) and the QIBA same-day pairs (right): median Dice similarity coefficient with the reference on the test scans (horizontal axis) and median test–retest ICC over the 107 features (vertical axis), with 95% CIs from a patient-level bootstrap. The dashed line marks the median ICC of the manual reference, and the dotted line in the QIBA panel the median inter-reader Dice. ICC = intraclass correlation coefficient.

Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and forest plots show classification by each mask source in IMD-CT (malignancy), LIDC-IDRI and LNDb (radiologist suspicion), DLCS24, and LUNA25-Dev (malignancy). Left, ROC curves as in Figure 6, with each AUC and its 95% CI below. Right, paired differences in AUC (first source minus second), with 95% CIs from a patient-level bootstrap with 2000 resamples on identical cross-validation splits, grouped by comparator: reference masks, log diameter, the Lung-RADS category (DLCS24), nnInteractive, and the reference-mask model applied to each method's features (deployed). Numbers give the difference, its 95% CI, and the Holm-adjusted two-sided bootstrap *P* value of the tests added after the results were known (Appendix S1); "*P* < .01" is the smallest value the resamples allow. Filled dots = *P* < .05, open dots = *P* ≥ .05, faded dots = not tested. Nonzero differences that round to 0.000 are shown with more decimals. A CI that includes 0 does not show equivalence. Diameter is not available for LUNA25-Dev. AUC = area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, CI = confidence interval.

Histograms show nodule diameter in each dataset and in all datasets combined (top left; 6563 nodules). Diameter is the maximal axial diameter of the reference segmentation, averaged over readers (RIDER-Seg: manual contour on the test scan; DLCS24: mean of the annotated box). Each panel gives the number of nodules and the median with IQR. Dashed lines mark 6, 8, 15, and 30 mm. LUNA25-Dev is not shown, because no nodule size with a documented source is available. IQR = interquartile range.

Receiver operating characteristic curves show the deployment analysis: the model trained on reference-mask features in each training fold, applied to each method's features in the test fold, in IMD-CT (malignancy), LIDC-IDRI, and LNDb (radiologist suspicion). Reference masks are black and the diameter model is dashed gray. Shaded bands are pointwise 95% CIs; the legend gives each AUC with its 95% CI from a patient-level bootstrap, in the order of the key. Missed nodules were scored at the training-fold prevalence. AUC = area under the receiver operating characteristic curve.

Grouped bar charts show performance at a target sensitivity of 90% for each mask source in IMD-CT, LIDC-IDRI, LNDb, DLCS24, and LUNA25-Dev. The threshold was set in each training fold of the patient-grouped fivefold cross-validation (three repeats) as the highest score that kept sensitivity at or above 90% and was applied unchanged to the test fold; values are from the pooled out-of-fold decisions, averaged over repeats. Bold numbers are point estimates; whiskers are 95% CIs from a patient-level bootstrap with 2000 resamples, with the bounds printed at the whisker ends (for short bars, the estimate and CI are printed above the bar). The dotted line marks the 90% target. Missed nodules were scored at the training-fold prevalence; because a threshold cannot split these tied scores, methods that missed many nodules reached a sensitivity of 0.97 to 1.00 with a specificity of 0.19 or less. Precision, F1 score, and accuracy depend on the proportion of positive nodules and should not be compared across datasets. Lung-RADS is not shown, because its categories could not target 90% sensitivity. Positive = malignant at histopathology (IMD-CT), suspicious to radiologists (LIDC-IDRI, LNDb), or from a patient with cancer (DLCS24, LUNA25-Dev). CI = confidence interval.

Dot plot shows Figure 5 at full width with feature names: the Lin concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) of each radiomic feature across nodules in QIBA, LIDC-IDRI, and LNDb. Dot size gives the percentage of nodules segmented, and an empty cell means fewer than five nodules were segmented. Colors, columns, and the right-hand summary are as in Figure 5. GLCM = gray-level co-occurrence matrix, GLDM = gray-level dependence matrix, GLRLM = gray-level run length matrix, GLSZM = gray-level size zone matrix, NGTDM = neighborhood gray-tone difference matrix.

Histograms show reference mask volume (milliliters, logarithmic scale) in each dataset with reference segmentations and in these datasets combined (top left), with the number of nodules and the median with IQR. IQR = interquartile range.

Heat maps show the volume ratio (top), 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95; middle), and diameter difference (bottom) of each method against the reference segmentation, by dataset. Cells give the median over segmented nodules, with 95% CIs from a patient-level bootstrap with 2000 resamples; for each nodule, the metric was averaged over reference outlines or masks. Volume ratio = method volume divided by reference volume; diameter difference = maximal axial diameter of the method mask minus that of the reference. Blue indicates a smaller and orange a larger mask than the reference (top and bottom), and darker orange a larger HD95 (middle). Colors are truncated at the ends of each color bar; printed values are not. \* Agreement between radiologists (QIBA, LIDC-IDRI, LNDb) or between the three QIN reference algorithms, each reference compared with the others and averaged; not computed for the diameter difference. NA = dataset with one reference segmentation per nodule.

Images show segmentation examples in LIDC-IDRI, one row per combination of attenuation (solid, part solid, ground glass) and size group (8 mm or less, more than 8 to 20 mm, more than 20 to 30 mm, more than 30 mm) that contains nodules. In each group, the nodule shown has the mean Dice over the eight methods (a miss counted as 0) closest to the group median, a rule fixed before any image was viewed. The first column shows the reference (consensus) outline in white; the other columns show each method's outline in color with the reference dashed. Labels give the Dice similarity coefficient and the volume ratio (VR, method over reference volume), or "No mask" when the method had no component within 5 mm of the nodule center. The number at upper left is the nodule diameter, with the nodule type below it where recorded.
Images show segmentation examples in LNDb, chosen and displayed as in Figure S5. The reference is the consensus outline.
Images show segmentation examples in QIBA, one row per size group (attenuation is not recorded), chosen and displayed as in Figure S5. The reference shows the outlines of the five radiologists.
Images show segmentation examples in IMD-CT, chosen and displayed as in Figure S5. The reference, labeled "Reader", is the nodule segmentation mask released with the dataset.
Images show segmentation examples in NSCLC-RG, chosen and displayed as in Figure S5. The reference is the expert segmentation.
